explanations.answer: Across to the other side of the lake
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” Clear plan, clear destination, no confusion. I've gotten turned around between my own counter and my own oven, so a plan that clean impresses me.

explanations.answer: Up onto the mountainside to pray
explanations.explanation: I get why you'd pick it, friend, but the text puts them on a boat. Jesus says, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” Nobody climbs a mountain in a boat, no matter how hard they row.

explanations.answer: Down along the riverbank to fish
explanations.explanation: This one's got water in it, so you're close. But the text says a lake, not a river, and it gives no fishing plan. Jesus says, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” That's the whole trip.

I see why you'd think so, since a nice boat ride is a fine time to stay up. But the text says, “As they sailed, He fell asleep…” So Jesus is asleep while they're still crossing. Awake the whole trip? Not this time.
Right on the money. The text says, “As they sailed, He fell asleep…” and then the windstorm comes down on the lake. So Jesus isn't awake the whole trip. He's asleep when the weather turns.
Yes, the disciples went and woke Him. The boat was being swamped and they were in great danger, so they went to the one who was asleep. Nobody sat there waiting for a better moment.

Close, but the text says the opposite. “The disciples went and woke Him…” The boat was being swamped, they were in great danger, and they didn't let Jesus keep sleeping. If my boat were filling up, I'd have been waking people too.
Yes, Jesus “…rebuked the wind and the raging waters…” Then they subsided, and all was calm. He doesn't sit and watch the storm. He gets up and speaks to it, and it settles.

I can see the thought, but that's not the word. The text says Jesus “…rebuked the wind and the raging waters…” That's a firm word, the kind you say when you mean it. After that, the waters subsided and all was calm.

Watching isn't what the text says. It says Jesus got up and “…rebuked the wind and the raging waters…” Then they subsided, and all was calm. He doesn't just sit through the storm. He gets up and speaks to it.

Yes, the text says, “Frightened and amazed, they asked one another…” The storm is gone, but the fear isn't. Calm water, shaken disciples. I think they'd just seen something they couldn't file away anywhere.

That one's not in the text. It says, “Frightened and amazed, they asked one another…” Anger isn't the word the text gives. It gives fear and amazement, and I think they were wondering about what they'd just watched.

The text doesn't say they felt ashamed. It says, “Frightened and amazed, they asked one another…” Jesus asked them, “Where is your faith?”, but their reaction is fear and amazement. I think they were still catching their breath.

Yes, they ask, “Who is this?” They keep going: “He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!” They've been in that boat with Him, and now they're asking who He is. That's a big question, and it's a good one.
The text has them asking something else. It says, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!” That question is about Jesus. It isn't about the route.

It's a fair question, but the text doesn't have them ask it. They ask one another, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!” They aren't asking about the nap. They're asking about Him.
Yes, the text says he “…stayed in the tombs.” No clothes and no house for a long time. That's a hard picture, and I think this one hurts.
Not the temple, friend. The text says, “…he stayed in the tombs.” It also says he had not worn clothing or lived in a house for a long time. I think that part is heavy.
No marketplace here. The text says he had not lived in a house, but he “…stayed in the tombs.” I think this part of the story is heavy, and it was a lonely place to stay.

explanations.answer: Son of the Most High God
explanations.explanation: Yes! He cries out, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?” He knows exactly who is standing in front of him, and he says it in a loud voice. The man is on the ground, but he gets the name right.

“Son of David” is a title people call Jesus in Matthew 9:27, but it's not what this man shouts. He says, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?” That's the name that comes out of him, loud and clear.

That's not the title here. The man shouts, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?” He falls down before Jesus and says it in a loud voice. Son of the Most High God is the name he uses.

Yes, “…he had broken the chains…” They were chains and shackles, and still they didn't hold him. The text says he was driven by the demon into solitary places. I think this part of the story is heavy.

They didn't hold. The text says that though he was bound with chains and shackles, “…he had broken the chains…” The demon drove him into solitary places. I think this one is heavy, so I'll say it plainly.
Nobody unlocked them. The text says, “…he had broken the chains…” They didn't hold him, and he was driven by the demon into solitary places. I think this is a heavy part of the story.
Yes, “…many demons had gone into him.” So when he says “Legion,” it's because there isn't just one. The name tells you the crowd inside him. Jesus asks, and the man answers plainly.
No soldiers in this scene. The text says he answered “Legion” because “…many demons had gone into him.” The name points to how many were in him. It's a heavy answer to a simple question.
That's not who went into him. The text says he said “Legion” because “…many demons had gone into him.” So the name tells you how many were in him. It's not about people at all.

explanations.answer: To let them enter the pigs
explanations.explanation: Yes, “…the demons begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs…” Right before that, the demons kept begging Jesus not to order them to go into the Abyss (Luke 8:31). A large herd of pigs was feeding on the hillside. That's what they asked about.

explanations.answer: To let them go to the tombs
explanations.explanation: The tombs aren't their request. The text says the demons “…begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs…” A large herd was feeding on the hillside, and that's what they asked about.

explanations.answer: To let them stay in the town
explanations.explanation: They don't ask for the town. The text says the demons “…begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs…” The herd was right there on the hillside. That's their request.

Yes, “…He gave them permission.” The demons begged to enter the pigs, and Jesus gave His permission (Luke 8:32). Nothing is hidden in that verse, so there's nothing to untangle. The text says it plainly, and so will I. True.
The text says the opposite. The demons begged to enter the pigs, “…and He gave them permission.” So Jesus did give permission. That makes this one True.

explanations.answer: Rushes into the lake and drowns
explanations.explanation: Yes, “…the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.” This happens after the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs. It's a hard scene, and the text tells it plainly. Then those tending the pigs ran off and reported it in the town and countryside.
That's not what happens. The text says “…the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.” They didn't scatter anywhere. They all went one direction, straight down the bank.

The town gets the news, but the herd never gets there. The text says “…the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.” It's the pig tenders who run off and report it in the town and countryside.
Yes, he's “…clothed and in his right mind…” Earlier he hadn't worn clothing for a long time. Now he's sitting at Jesus' feet, dressed and thinking clearly. What a change.
The text doesn't mention weeping. It says he's sitting at Jesus' feet, “…clothed and in his right mind…” Remember, he hadn't worn clothing for a long time. That's the change the text points out.
The text doesn't say he's praying. It says he's sitting at Jesus' feet, “…clothed and in his right mind…” After a long time without clothing, that's quite a change. I think the calm is the point.
Yes, “…they were afraid.” The people find the man sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind. I'd have expected cheering, but the text says fear. That's what they felt.

Not quite. The text says, “…they were afraid.” They came, found the man at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind, and fear is what they felt. It may not be the reaction you'd expect, but that's what the text says.

Yes, “…all the people of the region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them.” The text gives their fear as the reason. So Jesus got into the boat and started back. That's how this stop ends.
That's not what they ask. The text says they “…asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them.” They've just seen what He did for one man, and fear is what comes out.
They don't ask Him to stay and teach. The text says they “…asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them.” So Jesus got into the boat and started back.
I get why you'd think so, since the man begged to go with Jesus. But the text says, “…He sent him away…” The man asked, and Jesus gave him a different job instead. Staying home was part of the plan.
Yes, the man “…begged to go with Jesus. But He sent him away…” He doesn't get a seat in the boat. Jesus gives him a job at home instead.

explanations.answer: Go home and tell what God has done
explanations.explanation: Yes! Jesus says, “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” The man had just begged to go with Jesus, and Jesus sends him home instead. Home, where he lived among the tombs before, is where he gets to tell it. And he does, proclaiming all over the town how much Jesus had done for him.

explanations.answer: Go and tell no one what happened
explanations.explanation: It's the opposite. Jesus says, “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” He's sent to tell the story, and the man proclaims it all over the town.

explanations.answer: Go and show himself to the priest
explanations.explanation: That's not in this passage. Jesus says, “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” The man's job is telling the story back home, and he tells it all over the town.
